enumeration_note: One HTF-liquidity fade skeleton (mark untapped HTF level, drop to 5m/1m, tap + rejection confirmation, stop beyond level, 1:2 RR) taught with three compatible confirmation variants (single rejection, double bottom, failed-breakout trap). All fade the same direction at the level â€” no opposition â€” so grouped as one strategy with three variants.

coaching_notes: Most traders use liquidity wrong; find where the obvious/too-clean trades are sitting and do the opposite
Market makers push price into liquidity to fill large orders, so anticipate where price is going rather than react to it
The key is to look for clean price action that's just a little too clean â€” equal highs, trend lines, perfect-looking zones â€” that's the bait
Reversals happen fast and fake outs are fatal on the lower time frame
Always keep an eye out for the traps
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: first mark higher-time-frame (daily/4h) most-recent swing highs/lows and clean support/resistance levels that haven't been tapped yet
PRECONDITION: identify untapped HTF levels where liquidity should be living before dropping down
Drop to the 5-minute (or 1-minute) chart to time the entry
Wait for price to rapidly approach/tap a marked HTF level, ideally with a volume spike
Entry: fade the level (counter-trend) on rejection wick / bullish or bearish engulfing / exhaustion candle / long wick / volume divergence
Entry gate: do NOT enter before price taps the liquidity zone â€” wait for confirmation of the tap+rejection
Filter: do not chase breakouts â€” wait for price to trap traders and fade the move
Stop: below the session (London) low / just beyond the marked level
VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC: double bottom = two rejections of the same area with the bar not closing below the level
VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC: trap = wick above resistance then dump (short) / wick below support then reverse (long)
SESSION SELECTION: use London or New York open sessions â€” that is when the most stop hunts happen
strategies.entry_summary: First mark untapped higher-time-frame (daily/4h) swing highs/lows and clean support/resistance levels. Drop to the 5-minute (or 1-minute) chart, wait for price to rapidly approach and tap one of those marked levels (ideally with a volume spike), then enter a counter-trend fade off the level on a rejection wick / bullish or bearish engulfing candle / exhaustion candle / volume divergence. Do not enter before price taps the zone; prefer the London or New York open sessions.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop below the session (London) low / just beyond the marked level; target a 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio.
strategies.name: lower_tf_liquidity_fade

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: one tap of the level + rejection wick / engulfing candle (real-trade example used an engulfing candle with wicks then rejection up)
variants.target_note: 1:2 risk-to-reward, stop below current London low
variants.transcript_quote: we had rapid price movement to that zone, an engulfing candle, which both of these candles were with wicks and then we had that rejection up. That's when I was able to enter my trade at 61408 on Australian dollar. I kept my stop loss below the current London low and all I had to do was shoot for a 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: price rejects the same area twice with the bar not closing below the marked support level (full reversal)
variants.transcript_quote: if price rejects the same area twice, it could be a full reversal double bottom with the bar not closing below the area of support and resistance that you marked up and getting another trade 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: price wicks above resistance then dumps (short) or wicks below support then reverses (long) â€” the stop-hunt wick beyond the level is the confirmation
variants.transcript_quote: Price will often wick above resistance, pause, then dump or wick below support and reverse. That is your confirmation.
